FLASHCARD SET · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Colors & Shades flashcards.

Fifteen spotter sheets, sixty labeled things, one color at a time. Each card gathers four things that share a color — the red apple, the yellow sun, the grey elephant, the gold trophy — so a child meets the color word four times before moving on. The first eleven cards are the colors toddlers name first; the last four are the shades older kids can mix themselves: light blue, navy, peach and lavender. Every card page carries a simple guide — what the color is, where it hides in your house, and one way to hunt it tonight.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page, and every card shows its age pill — start with the group that fits your child today.

The first colors

The eleven colors a child names first, in the deck’s own order: the red apple to the gold honey pot. Four labeled things on every card — name the color, then hunt it in the room.

More colors (ages 4-5)

Four shades for bigger spotters — each one a color you can MAKE: light blue is blue plus white, navy is blue gone dark, peach is orange gone soft, lavender is purple gone pale.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    The color hunt

    Pick one card, then hunt its color all day — clothes, cups, cars, cushions. Every find is a point, said out loud: "red car, two!" The deck turns the whole house into the game.

  2. 02

    Sixty things, one floor

    Lay all the cards face up. Sixty labeled things sit there — a whale, a pretzel, a koala, a crown. Ask: "what on this floor is red?" and watch the sorting begin.

  3. 03

    I spy, card edition

    Hold up three cards and spy something in the room that matches one of them. "I spy with my little eye… something GOLD." The trophy card wins when the door handle does.

  4. 04

    Mix talk

    The shade cards are made, not found: blue plus white makes light blue, blue plus a night sky makes navy. Ask "how do you think they MADE this one?" — that is real color theory, age four style.

  5. 05

    One color a day

    Read one card at breakfast — a twenty-second color visit. At that pace the deck lasts three weeks, and every color gets its own morning.
